utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence wanted to raise a preliminary matter. But before we do that, I apologise for the late start. I apologise, not the Chamber. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We have several open issues, and one of them is that the Prosecution, on October the 1st, on transcript pages 39612, line 24, to 39613, line 3, said and gave us the ERN range numbers that should correspond now to D1243, and we said that we didn't see the whole document, and only pages from that document, 5 to 8, 10, 11, and 13 from that range were disclosed to the Defence previously. So only after the Prosecution uploaded 33 -- 65 ter 33168 we have the rest of the document. We checked on EDS and that's what we could find. Next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you remind me what it was. Because you'll understand that I have no recollection just on the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we're discussing the Vase Miskina shelling file from the 27th of May, 1992. I do believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way -- and, Mr. Lukic, this was your first item?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps it's better to immediately hear from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution, as we've indicated before, is happy to sit down with counsel and go through the records. We -- this hasn't been discussed with us, so we're happy to go through our disclosures and everything, these are similar matters, and direct them to where the materials were disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they were disclosed. Because that's the issue, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, but if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- you do that and then we'll hear whether there is still a disclosure issue or not. Next one, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next item is video that we did not have ERN number. It's 1D05916 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Video of?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Video of -- it's compilation of Markale and Dobrinja, I think, and there is something from the later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's the video. I see you have it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you want to give it to the Registry. And was a number assigned already? You'll understand that not knowing what the 65 ter number -- the ERN number or -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that the number assigned was D1267.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar confirms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, again -- I mean, I'm not sure if these are all going to be in the same vein, but we're happy to discuss with counsel, and that we wanted just verification of the ERN for it. And I know that Mr. Lukic's colleague has informed me that the video might have presented in court, thereby without an ERN, and there was a transcript reference. So if there's transcript reference, that's all we're really waiting for just so we could verify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can do even better. We have ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's V000-8939. And it came through Sead Besic and was tendered through Turkusic, Emir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I guess I'm a bit confused if counsel is saying that the video is already tendered and admitted. But aside from that, we're happy to check the video that was played against that ERN, and if there's any difficulties we'll re-raise it with the Chamber. I don't want to unnecessarily hold up counsel's exhibits, so we will raise that independently if that's an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lukic, you said it was tendered. It wasn't admitted. What's the status of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just have the reference that it was tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that it was admitted, or I take it then provisionally admitted if there's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably some portions. Not the portions we played lately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then what we then should do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the 65 ter number? That would help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I do understand that the matter was dealt with on the 30th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And most likely, but I'm speaking on behalf of the authority of Madam Registrar, the 65 ter number -- the doc ID would be 1D05916.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the 65 ter number. And the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is 1267, yes. So what you then, as a matter of fact, wish, Mr. Lukic, is that you wanted the existing video be replaced by the newly uploaded one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand 1267, is it 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's -- D1267 is an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we will replace the existing one with a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I guess what caused me confusion in Mr. Lukic's statement was that the reference to being previously tendered, and I believe Mr. Lukic indicated it was Mr. Turkusic, which was quite a while ago, that's when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's my information that it was done with Mr. Besic on 30th of September. Then I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was, I do understand, 30th September. Of course, Ms. Subotic was -- was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart has kindly provided some additional information. It appears that some of this video, just to put the pieces together, was tendered with Mr. Turkusic as Exhibit D352. Previously. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was previously and then it was more portions then, or at least another selection was tendered, with Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's not clear right now to the Prosecution the exact whole time of what's being tendered now, so if we could just verify what portions are that would be just appreciated and with that we can go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what we'll do is if you hand over, or perhaps you have done that already, the video, then within the next 48 hours we'd like to hear the result of your short conversation with Mr. Weber. We'll then also hear from Mr. Weber whether there's any objection against this new version of most likely D1267.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We -- I noticed that I did not offer into evidence our exhibits on the first day, so I have that list with me, or you want me to do the whole thing with Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- how long is the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Seven, eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would -- then I would suggest that you -- when you meet anyhow with Mr. Weber, that he considers whether or not there's any objection, you read the numbers and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not sure what the exact list is. If we could have it. We've had full discussions over the exhibits from the list last Friday about what we do not oppose, so if -- I don't know to what degree the current list incorporates that, but that's the current status, it's my understanding, of where those discussions are at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you check whether your exhibits are the ones, the non-opposables. If so, you can just read them into the record and then we'll deal with it very quickly. If there's anything else, then I will hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I'll wait to discuss it with Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we hear from you preferably this week. These were the matters you wanted to raise. Could the witness then be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Fluegge reminds me that "this week" means not later than tomorrow, because we have -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I was concerned about. I don't know if we are going to -- whether we will be able to finish everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, I remind you, you know the routine, although it's a routine with a meaning, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You made the calculations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's highly appreciated. Could you give them to the usher. And then if the parties would not object, the Chamber would have a look at it and then it will be distributed. Please proceed, meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning again, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The 122-millimetre Grad rocket is designed to be launched from a multi-barrel rocket-launcher; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The 122-millimetre Grad rocket has no guidance system; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Grad is just a nickname. The more formal name for the 122-millimetre Grad rocket is the M-21-OF; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the Karadzic testimony, at transcript page 38484, you were asked: "Q. Right. Well, I'm going to put this to you that rockets are not designed to be fired simultaneously. They're designed to be fired in a salvo, which is to say consecutively, albeit with extremely short durations of time between the exit of each rocket from the MBRL?" Your answer: "Well, we're discussing this all this time. This is what I told you to start with, didn't I? "So you'll agree with that assertion," was the next question. Your answer was: "That's what I already said at the beginning." Do you stand by this testimony.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: By rockets being fired in a salvo, there's a distance created between each rocket in the air, correct, since they are fired consecutively?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minimal. If a salvo is being fired you choose the number of rockets that you are going to fire. And then through the firing system, that is regulated. If three or four are being fired, salvos, conditionally speaking, then it is a very small time distance, if we can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The amount of impulsive force is different if an air bomb is propelled by one rocket, three rockets, or four rockets; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is different. The total impulsive force, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Given that we are dealing with rockets of different numbers and air bombs of different weights, the total mass of each modified air bomb in each variety is different; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every construction solution has a different mass, individually speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Given there was a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, sorry to interrupt you, but earlier you said aerial bombs to be fired. It was my understanding that you drop aerial bombs from planes and that, therefore, you don't fire them but you release them and that they -- so I'm a bit puzzled by what you said about firing aerial bombs if not mounted with rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I -- I don't know if Your Honour is referring to line 24 of page 8. But I meant to be saying in that that when asking if the air bomb is propelled by the rockets, so referring to then a modified -- it being -- the air bomb being attached with a rocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because earlier you said they are not -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was a little bit further back that you ... let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe my earlier question might have been with respect to the rockets, not necessarily the air bomb. I don't know if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By rockets being fired in a salvo -- let me just see. Yes, it's all about rockets and not about ... yes, I now better understand where I went wrong. But if you are talking about rockets attached to an aerial bomb, then if that's what you mean, or rockets being fired separately apart from being mounted on an aerial bomb, then it may become clearer for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will keep that in mind. I was earlier referring just the rockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just the rockets. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, given that there was a different combination of mass and propulsive force for each of the configurations of modified air bombs, the ballistic properties for each of the configurations was different; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not correct. Each individual one went within a technical solution. It's not that every one of them went individually. There were FAB-100s and FAB-200s. The 100 had three motors and 250 had three and four motors, so these were separate technical solutions. It's not that each and every one of them was different. Each and every modified air bomb, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that Ms. Subotic should answer again since everything was not recorded correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any doubt in that respect -- Could you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- repeat your answer. I noticed that at least the FAB-200 -- FAB-200 a little bit later were FAB-250.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's even correct but for 100 it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you repeat what you said about the FAB-100.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I said it's not true that each bomb had its own design, its own technical solution. Within certain technical solutions there existed FAB-100, which had one rocket or three; and FAB 200, which had a three-motor or four-motor option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D5497; page 222 in the B/C/S and page 246 in the English. And we may need to rotate the image. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is what appears to be a thrust diagram for a 122-millimetre Grad rocket from Appendix 2 of your modified air bomb report. The information in this chart is for a single Grad rocket; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my lab which tested these Grad rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this chart, the propulsive force of a Grad rocket is used up in about 1.8 seconds; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree that it would be vitally important to ensure the accuracy of an air bomb, if it is modified with multiple rockets attached to it, that each of the rockets ignite at exactly the same moment?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's say -- and I want to direct you back to this chart. Let's say there is an air bomb with four rockets attached it, and one of the rockets were to ignite .4 of a second after the other three. This one rocket would still be burning .4 of a second after the other three stop burning; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hypothetically, it's true. However, such a rocket does not exist. It doesn't pass the checks, the tests, and there are a series of tests measuring the time of ignition and the time of burning. These tests are made on every series of motors and these never pass assembly. .4 would be extremely high. You see how much it is. It's 20 per cent of the total burning. It's absolutely out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, if we could stay focused. According to your graph with .4 seconds left in the fuel tank, the impulsive force being driven on the modified air bomb from, let's say, that one last rocket is still going to be 25.000 newtons down to 0; right? That's what this chart would indicate?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this chart shows what kind of propulsion force a regular Grad motor has, what its burning is like, how the propulsive force develops in the chamber, and how it disperses during the burning. It doesn't show anything like what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the Karadzic case at transcript page 38494, a question was put to you: "I want to put it to you that after -- with 0.4 seconds left in the fuel tank, if you like, the impulsive force being driven on the modified air bomb system by that one rocket that is still going is by your own graph 25.000 Newtons decreasing down to 0. Do you accept that?" You answered: "Yes, that is indeed the case." That was your previous testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that previously, but that's a hypothetical proposition. Such a thing does not exist. Such a thing does not happen. Because a motor like that does not ever get through to assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid, to the extent I understand the discussion, you're talking at cross-purposes. Mr. Weber presents a chart in which the development of the propelling power is shown and then asked questions about the consequences if the rockets are not ignited exactly at the same time. You're saying it doesn't say anything about that because you do not accept that it could happen that they do not ignite at the same time. And that's the reason why you say it's all hypothetical, because it wouldn't have passed assembly. Now you can go on for a long time to do this, but the core therefore is two questions: First, how precise is the simultaneously -- is the ignition simultaneous, is it really exactly the same time; and if not, what are the consequences for the trajectory or at least for the flight path. I think these are the two core questions Mr. Weber wants to touch upon. If you try to understand that and not say it has got nothing to do with it, because it has something to do it, irrespective of whether it would have passed assembly. If the ignition is not accurately simultaneous, then, of course, that may have consequences, I take it. You say that doesn't exist. Mr. Weber is putting questions about that situation. I think -- I tried to find out how much you were in cross-purposes. I hope you both are now on the same line again so that we can receive useful testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Absolutely synchronised ignition of a modified air bomb with three to four rockets is impossible to achieve; correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see that the transcript refers says "absolutely ignition." I was referring to "absolutely synchronised ignition."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, ma'am. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Synchronised ignition is precisely defined by designed documentation, and its tolerances are determined in such a way that it has no influence on dispersion at target.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the Karadzic case your co-author, Mr. Poparic, testified at transcript page 39038 to the following: "Q. The modified air bombs with three and four rockets required absolutely synchronous ignition of those rockets; correct?" His answer: "Absolutely synchronised ignition does not exist; it's impossible to achieve." He then went on to explain the requirements. Do you agree with Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33191 for the witnesses. And if we could please just have one of the images in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is a photograph that was taken by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor on 19 April 1996 in Vogosca. We see that there's four rocket motors attached in a manner that they were supposed to be used with a modified air bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really see four motors here linked into one whole, but I don't see a bomb. It's possible they were used, but I cannot see that from this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For a modified air bomb to be attached with a rocket system like the one we see here, it would be important, if not vital, that each rocket is connected in a manner that is exactly parallel to each other rocket; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Another thing if you're going to connect this to an air bomb, the assembly that we see here would have to be exactly parallel to the air bomb itself; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relative to the horizontal axis of the air bomb, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go into the -- focus in on the -- let's take the rear part of the upper right rocket. We are zoomed into the rear part of one of the rockets. Do you see the pieces of metal that are underneath what appears to be a -- I'll describe it as a greyish/green metal band?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is a metal band, I see something greyish/green and it does look like a band.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you, with the assistance of the usher, take care that the cursor moves in such a way that we know exactly what you're talking when you're talking about the metal band.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure. If the -- if the court usher could please go to the right -- to the back end of the rocket that's visible on the screen. To the back end of it, please. To --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the far end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, to the far right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The back is where the -- where the seven circles are --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or the seven dark spots. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. So right there do you see what appears to be -- I'm going to describe it as a piece of metal underneath what -- a band on the rocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that where the cursor is now at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, at the top of what I'm referring to as a piece of metal, underneath the band.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that piece of metal is then where. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's right on it. Now it just moved off it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see just a little bit up, then. There it is? Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nope, a little off. If you're following the circle -- there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There it is. Okay. Please proceed. Perhaps it later could be marked, so let's keep the picture as it is at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you see what I'm referring to? What I'm directing to you -- is that the stabiliser of the rocket that's fastened under -- that's fastened what is a band, what I'm describing as a band?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't see that from this position on this kind of photograph. Yes, there is something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender the photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photograph is not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, in order to understand what we're talking about, it's good that that portion will be marked. Now, you can invite the witness to do so, but it should be clear then that it's not her expression of the marking --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because she has the pen and she's in control at this moment. Mr. Usher, could you please assist the witness. Witness, it's perfectly clear that it's not primarily your testimony but that you mark the area where the cursor is now and that it only reflects where the cursor was at the time. You make perhaps a little cross. A tiny little cross there. No, could you -- no. Could you erase that, Mr. Usher. Witness the only thing is a tiny little cross at the spot where the cursor was a second ago and where the pen is now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, this is up. It's not exactly the same place, as a matter of fact. It is -- could it -- could it be erased again. Mr. Usher, perhaps you -- yes. I think that was the spot, if all parties agree. Yes, that's then the little blue cross. That's where the witness marked where the cursor was a second ago, and it's not her own that it's -- means anything. Please, Madam Registrar, the number would be for this enlarged zoomed in photograph marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7562, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I could also tender the full photo, 65 ter 33191 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We want this to be separate exhibits, yes. Madam Registrar the full photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The full photograph of document 33191 receives Exhibit P7563, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Modified air bombs were launched on rails; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These modified air bombs were launched from a rail launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could step by step, please. The length of the rails impacts the precision of the modified air bomb. For example, a rail that is 25 metres long will be more precise than one that is 4 to 6 metres long; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's quite enough to secure the whole length of the bomb together with a motor, plus one length. That's quite enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll ask if you confirm a part of your previous testimony at page 38498 in the Karadzic case: "Q. Well, it looks like we've reached agreement that the length of the rails will have an impact on the precision?" Your answer was: "Yes, on the precision, but this has no bearing on the range whatsoever."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the problem is that the witness doesn't answer your question. The witness says what she thinks is enough, whereas your question was whether 25 metres would be better than 4 to 6 metres. So therefore, Witness, if you would please answer the questions. That saves a lot of time. Do you agree that a rail of 25 metres would give more precision than a rail that is 4 to 6 metres long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why exactly 25 metres. I can't understand that. It's very important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to understand that. The question simply is whether it gives more precision, not in range but in the direction of firing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Higher precision in terms of dispersion of target, that could be. But not necessarily. It's not a pre-condition. They just provide a more secure start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means a more secure flight path, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The thing is, it would positively influence the reduction of impulse at start that the rocket has when it leaves the rail launcher. In the beginning of flight of any projectile, there are disturbances at the beginning that affect precision. This perhaps could be favourable because it could reduce these initial disturbances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 167 of your modified air bomb report, you state: "It was assumed that the average range of bombs was 6.000 metres." This was the base-line distance you used for the range of a modified air bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the basic distance for which we determined precision. That is the distance at which we defined precision and conducted further analyses because, of course, we were in a position to determine exact distances of firing in the incidents that we analysed. For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Since it appears you say that the average range of bombs was 6.000 metres, would it be correct that the angle of elevation of the rails would either increase or decrease the range of the modified air bomb and the distance it travels to the target?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The start angle is always a parameter that is closely related to range.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. So if the rails would be either raised or lowered, that would affect whether the modified air bomb could possibly travel, according to you, more than 6.000 metres or less than 6.000 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your report, it appears that you take issue with Berko Zecevic's calculations for modified air bomb of between 4800 and 6800 metres. The fact is your assumed range falls within the ranges provided by Mr. Zecevic, and actually Mr. Zecevic's ranges appear to be a bit conservative compared to yours; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What you just said is a conflation. In our analysis, we made analysis of precision for an average range. That's one kind of range. There is a point in our report where we contested the analyses of Mr. Zecevic, and they refer to ricochet start angles, ricochet angles on the ground, the exact co-ordinates at sites that he referred to, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Those are different things. I was just focusing on the range that he says. You agree that your average range falls within the ranges that he calculated; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also dealt with ranges of 8.000 metres and various other ranges. Maybe at one place we coincided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, why don't you answer the question? The question is about a range given by Mr. Zecevic between 4800 and 6800, whether the range you calculated - that is, 6.000 plus or minus - falls within that range. That was the simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is simple but it's not correctly put because it's not the same analysis. He was not contested on the ranges he proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you are contesting - and that's apparently what your answer implies - that Mr. Zecevic calculated the range between 4800 and 6800, then we'll check that or Mr. Weber will put it to you, perhaps now or later, that that is what Mr. Zecevic says. And if you then says he does not, then at least we know where the difference of you is. Please proceed, Mr. Weber. Yes, I saw you looking at the clock. I should have done that. Let's take a break, and the witness may follow the usher. And we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I did further confirmation and checking over the break on what Mr. Zecevic listed as the effective range for the modified air bombs. For a FAB-100, it was 4.145 to 5.560 metres, and the effective range of a FAB-250 as 5.820 to 7.680 metres, and this is being based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that anywhere in evidence before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. It's based on his testimony and -- well, Your Honours, I believe that there are some adjudicated facts that relate to range of modified air bombs which may be based in part upon this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the difference in range is the result of the angle of firing or.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That -- that -- that is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will not deliver its judgement on the basis of the understanding of the OTP if --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would -- I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So please try to be precise in that respect. Mr. Weber, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, a fully assembled modified air bomb as well as the launch systems for the modified air bombs would have to have had to be manufactured under tightly controlled factory conditions and thoroughly tested before being approved for use; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In order to fire any modified air bomb with accuracy, you would need detailed firing tables; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nowhere in your report do you refer to contemporaneous test data from 1994 or 1995 for modified air bombs or the system used to launch it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That was not the subject of this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you accept that a modified air bomb could be off target by at least - and I'll just use this as a figure - 250 metres in any direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in any direction. There are exact calculations involved and probably certain deviations, and we'd have to know in some of these deviations are larger and in other cases they are smaller, so we'd have to take a look. It's that kind of a system. We'd have to see what kind of range we're looking at and what this is all about. In principle that can happen, but again it's not in any direction. Just one. That would probably be the biggest deviation that could be found in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to understand. In every direction I understand to be the left, to the right, short, and long. You said it could be found not in any direction. Just one. Which one? Or would you say that it never would go -- which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say, and I thought that I was precise enough, it behaves differently during flight depending on the range. Deviation in terms of direction and in terms of distance. It cannot be that big in both ways. It's either in terms of distance or in terms of direction. That's the nature of the system. That is how the forces work. That is how the flight takes place. I never saw anything that big, but let's say it's up to 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now let me to try to understand. You say it's either the direction or the range. Do I understand you well that if there's a deviation in the range - that is, that it's short or longer - that it couldn't deviate to the left and to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, not to that extent. Perhaps to a smaller extent. It's not going to be 200 left, 200 right, 200 front, 200 back. If it is range, then it is considerably less in terms of direction and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any data or tables for -- or any outcome of research on that, for the specific modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, I have told you. I had tables in my hands from 1990-something and 2002, so, yes, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are firing tables which is something not exactly the same as research on deviation. My question is: Do you have not what you once had in your hands, but do you have any reliable documentation on the deviations either in the -- in short, long, left, or right, any test results or whatever, so that we can look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The results of the testing were certainly included in firing tables. They're always attained in an experimental way. They're not being calculated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we don't have the firing tables. You once had them in your hands. And now I'm asking you whether you have any of these test results, and you say you can't produce them. You don't have them so that we can look at them. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a follow-up. What Mr. Weber asked you was whether the deviation could be 250 metres. You say no it could be less. How much less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I saw up to 200, 210. But again, I'm saying not at the same time in the same range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber's question didn't include time. He just asked whether you accept that the deviation would 250 metres in any direction. You're saying no, not 250. 200, 210. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then just for my understanding, it could be 200 metres to the left or 200 metres to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which then covers 400 metres; or on 210 metres, 420 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now short and long, the same? Also 200 to 2140 metres short or 200 and 210 metres long.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of range, I think a bit less. Because the very characteristic of forces of reaction leads to more dispersion in terms of direction. The bigger the range is, the smaller the dispersion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any documentary test results so that we can look at those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not except for those tables I said you could ask for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just understand one thing. Ma'am, you're talking of dispersion. Does an air bomb disperse or does it -- is it just one solid thing that falls on a particular object, a particular target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Air bombs are solid and they fall on a certain target. When speaking of dispersion, it has to do with a surface. Say if we fire seven or eight projectiles in the same direction, and then we are talking about that dispersion. And then when we're talking about deviation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm talking about one bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we're talking about 1. -- yes, one bomb, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So one bomb, does disperse or does it hit a target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "dispersion," I'm talking about possible deviation in terms of where the bomb will fall in relation to the desired target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, so you mean "deviation," then that's a different story. Thank you so much. I understand you better now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that is a characteristic of dispersion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D5497, page 199 of the B/C/S and page 218 of the English translation. And could I please have the B/C/S version rotated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before is table 5 from your modified air bomb report in this case, which is -- follows as part of paragraph 167 of your report where you indicate you assume the average range of modified air bombs was 6.000 metres. I would like to discuss a few of the entries with you. First, column number 5 is entitled: "Deviation from target." In this column, you entered what you considered to be the distance from a probable target that you felt was there to the point where the projectile impacted; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Going down the column to number 8, it appears that you list the impact at Cobanija number -- I'm sorry to the row, not column. Number 8. It appears that you list the impact at Cobanija number 7 as being 490 metres from an army command. At number 14, the point of impact appears to be 250 metres from what you considered to be a business commercial centre. Assuming these distances are accurate - and just for the record we -- the Prosecution isn't conceding that they are - and the type of projectiles you list impact at these locations, these are instances where modified air bombs were off target by at least 250 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I have to note something here. We intentionally put Cobanija 7 there, that is, as you can see, 490, in order to give the most unfavorable case. If you remember, what we established there was that not a single air bomb was there. Rather, that there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- a staging that took place. It didn't fall there but we dealt with it so that it would not seem that we did not want to include something that was unfavorable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm focusing on your chart. We'll eventually admit the investigative materials and let the Chamber deduce what happened. But I want to just -- for these two entries, the 490 at Cobanija and the 250 that you list in row 14, would these entries -- would these have been overshoots, undershoots, wide left, or wide right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know? No. It didn't go too far, too close, too much to the left, too much to the right. Just look at 6 and 7 here. These are columns that speak about probable --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm focusing on two entries: Entry on line 8 and entry on line 14. Let's take very specifically line 8. Was this an overshoot, an undershoot, wide right, or wide left?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. I think that Ms. Subotic answered number 8 already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In cross-examination, certainly under the present circumstances, you can put a question twice and it's still questionable whether she answered the question. Please proceed, and you may answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If this was a -- if this was an impact, as you indicate in this chart, would this have been an overshoot, an undershoot, wide left, or wide right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the only projectile out of these 16 that were analysed that had a deviation that was more than 3, according to tables. And in artillery, left, right, overshoot, undershoot, that is considered to be standard deviation that is permissible. That is a characteristic of a system that is satisfactory as far as ballistics is concerned. So a normal deviation is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not catch what.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the only projectile that left this border, if you will, and that can be seen on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And now you should answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you now please answer the question. It was 490 metres off target. Which direction. Left, right, overshoot, undershoot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't have that information here, whether it's an overshoot, undershoot. I mean, in the table that is. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you gave us a long answer, whereas apparently you now are telling us you don't know. Just tell us that right away that you don't know. That's fine. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that an acceptable deviation for a modified air bomb is 490 metres in any given direction?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For any artillery system, regardless of whether it's a mortar system, an artillery system, or a rocket artillery system, 3 VV plus/minus and 3 VD plus/minus are acceptable deviations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. So are you saying then that's an acceptable deviation for a modified air bomb? That's what you're saying; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm saying no for 8, because it probably went beyond that. And it's best for us to analyse it according to the circular one in column 8. And that is the only analysed bomb out of the 16 that went beyond normal ballistic expectations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's take number 14. The 250 metres, was that an overshoot, undershoot, wide right, wide left, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Circular deviation within 2 and 3 deviations in terms of a circular direction. Now, I would have to know exactly on the map whether it was overshoot or undershoot. I would have to look at that case. It would be best to discuss what is in column 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your short answer would be: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the question is repeated for me, I will respond by saying "I don't know." The answer I provided is the one that I thought was appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you find 250 metres to be an acceptable deviation for a modified air bomb?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all rules and regulations of the profession, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's focus a little bit more here. In columns 6, 7, and 8 of the table, you include values for different variables under the heading of "Probable Table Deviation." These are values that you selected, correct, for the FAB-250s and the FAB-100 modified air bombs?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is experimental data taken from the firing tables for FAB-100 and FAB-250 for analysing a range of 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I -- let's -- let's define things here. The VD -- I don't accept that these come from the firing tables, but I want to go through your chart nonetheless. Let's define what we're talking about here. The VD is a value for the dispersion of hits according to distance. VP is the dispersion of hits according to direction. Probable deviation is a measure of the dispersion of hits whose value in metres is calculated so that it is equally probable that half the hits are less than and the other half greater than this value. You agree that these are the standard meanings of these values; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are probable deviations according to direction and according to range, and this is probably circular deviation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's just see if we can go through some examples. In column 6 for the VD --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain briefly again what is circular deviation is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is precisely what the Prosecutor, Mr. Weber, referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is perhaps that ... let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In column 6 for the VD of the modified air bombs, you indicate the 100 and 250 kilograms varieties all had the same value: 43 metres. And in this chart, you have no indication whatsoever of the rocket composition or the angle of fire. Do you really think that the values would be exactly the same for air bombs of different weights with differing amounts of rockets being fired at different angles? This would not be the case; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. You're right. Special cases were dealt with here. They were analysed and information was provided for them; that is to say, if we established that there's a FAB involved with three motors, then that is the information contained here. And if it was established that it is FAB-250 with three motors, then again - here we had these cases, mostly - we provided that information. It has nothing to do with the angle if we defined range, so we gave it all for one range. There is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness slowly state her last question [sic]. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is different for 6 kilometres for the other bomb. So information was provided for specific cases in accordance with firing tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You understand that the variables for mortars are different in the mortar firing tables depending on size and the type of mortar, its weight, the number of charges, and the angle of fire? You must realise that; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. That is an elementary thing, professionally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have inserted values here that are not much greater than the deviations for a mortar; for example, an M62 P3 120-millimetre light mortar fired on charge 6 at its lowest angle has a VD of 38 metres. It's not credible that you are asserting here that modified air bombs were about as accurate as mortars; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything can be convincing for you or anything cannot be convincing for you. You're not in your own field. I have a honourable proposition for you and the Trial Chamber: Do write a request for the firing tables. They will probably provide that to you, and you will find that information there. I am not lying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not seeking your advice. We're seeking your answers to the questions that are put to you, and one of -- the last questions was, whether you -- it's your view - although that was expressed slightly different - whether it was credible or not credible that modified air bombs were about as accurate as mortars. Could you please answer that question, whether the position -- the accuracy is the -- approximately the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The precision approximately is not the same. But if it coincided with regard to this range, then it is exactly what is contained here in the table. It was exactly taken over from the firing tables. It was obtained on the basis of research, and there is no mistake involved here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm slightly confused. You said the data you have taken from firing tables. Which firing tables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firing tables from 2002, compiled by the institute in 2002. And there is detailed testing and research involved of all the equipment, including these bombs, before they were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we are talking about weapons used during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Technically it is more or less the same weapon, as far as the technical design is concerned. There is no particular effect in differences in construction with regard to the flight. I think that that model that was presented in 2001 is something that I attached to one of my previous papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, do you have the detailed fabrication -- the detailed sketches, the material for those bombs that were produced during the war? Do you have the -- the -- as technicians do, they have details, centimetres, millimetres, material, et cetera? Do you have them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's very difficult for you to be -- to accurately compare the -- what was produced during the war with what was produced after the war. It's only a general comparison rather than a detailed comparison. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to translate your evidence a little further here, and I'll take the values that you have for the -- for a FAB-250 modified air bomb and try to put it to you in lay terms. According to these valuations, you are saying that there is a 50 per cent chance that a FAB 250 modified air bomb fired from 6 kilometres away would land in an elliptical area of 154 metres by 86 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear the beginning of the question. FAB-250?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm taking is -- let's just focus on row 1. You have -- for a FAB-250, you have a VD of 43 and a VP of 77. So that would translate, according to these values -- what you're saying is that there is a 50 per cent chance that a FAB-250 modified air bomb fired from 6 kilometres away would land in an elliptical area of 154 metres by 86 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see here some data that doesn't fit in with your reckoning. I said that 50 per cent should fall within a circle of a 270 diameter if we look at column 8. But if we look at column 7 and 6, those are 3 VV to -- ahead and 3 VP to the left and right. So in the first case we are talking about all fired projectiles, and in the second case 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not looking to go into Gaussian discussions with you here. I'm just asking for a simple one variable distance, okay? And this -- this was gone through with your colleague in the past. So the elliptical area that would be covered, according to this, would be in 154 metres by 86 metres, and 50 per cent of the hits, according to what you're saying in this chart, would land inside that elliptical area and 50 per cent would land outside; right? And this is standard stuff in the firing tables. You're nodding your head. If you could please give a verbal response.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have to wait for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Don't be impatient.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33201, page 12 of the B/C/S. And if we could just enlarge this one because there's lot of information on the one table for the witness to see. And if we could -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. This is the firing table for the M21-OF, as you've acknowledged, known as the Grad rocket of 122-millimetres. I'd like to go on this table to about seven rows down, the row starting with the figure 6.000 on the left-hand side. You agree that according to this chart that a 122-millimetre Grad rocket fired from 6.000 metres has a VD of 202 metres and the VP of 43 [sic] metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has a VP of 34 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's what I said. So you agree that the VD is 202 metres and the VP is 34 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I heard in my headset 43 metres. That's why I corrected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this if you're firing a fully tested 122-millimetre Grad rocket from a fully tested rocket-launcher located 6.000 metres from a target, there's a 50 per cent chance that the rocket will land within an ellipse which is 404 metres by 68 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report in table 5 that we just looked at, what it appears that you're saying is that both FAB-100 and FAB-250 modified air bombs, regardless of their configuration, launched from a modified rail launcher, were far more accurate than the 122-millimetre Grad rocket when it was just fired on its own as intended; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The results that we presented are a bit different. We had 50 per cent more dispersion by direction, compared to Grad, and half the dispersion by length -- by range, by distance. There is a great influence of the aerodynamic shape on the velocity of a projectile, and one should not forget that we talking here about subsonic projectiles which are far more precise than the type of Grad, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure you're answering my question. What you're saying in your table 5 of your report is that modified air bombs - FAB-100, FAB-250 - regardless of their configuration in terms of number of rockets are far more accurate than a 122-millimetre Grad rocket when it's just fired on its own; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of my sentence, I said, and I don't see why you are neglecting it, the precision per direction at 5 kilometres in modified air bombs is almost 30 per cent less than the Grad rocket, and the precision -- I wanted to say more. We have 43 and 48, and here we see 34; whereas, in terms of range, it is more precise. That is to say, less dispersion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, at the end, the surface of where the rockets or the modified air bomb would land, is it smaller for the rockets, or is it smaller for the modified air bombs? What area where they are likely to fall with the 50-per cent rule, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Grad would fall into an ellipsoid of a length 404 metres and 68 metres wide, whereas an air bomb FAB-250 would --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness stop here and slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, first of all, you're invited to slow down. Second, my simple question was: The surface of which of the two ellipsis is larger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be larger with Grad at 6.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which then means that the aerial bombs would be more accurate than the Grad rocket if fired separately, individually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. Those are the results in the firing tables for Grad and the firing tables for modified air bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that was the gist of the question by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your evidence that Grad rockets somehow became more accurate and almost as accurate as any projectile possible by adding large 100-kilogram and 250-kilogram air bombs to them is not credible. Do you really expect us to believe that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the record, I have to say this: I am talking about the Grad rocket, meaning the complete Grad rocket, the whole system whose firing tables were shown to me; whereas, the second thing we are talking about are modified air bombs with a Grad rocket motor. I don't want to leave any confusion. I don't want anyone to understand me as if I had said something about the Grad rocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question. The question is whether the -- I'll not repeat the question. You have heard it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I heard the question. It's all right. Experiments show that that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please -- please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if you've looked at the tables for a 120-millimetre Grad rocket, but are you aware that, according to these tables, that a Grad rocket is not recommended to be fired on distances under 5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are safety systems with all systems, safety precautions and safety recommendations for all systems of rocket artillery. I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, please answer the question. Don't tell us what exists elsewhere. Just answer the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would ask that 65 ter 33201 be marked for identification. We do have to complete a translation for this specific table that's in front of Your Honours, but I see the other translations are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, what number would the table receive.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is marked for identification. We're not there yet, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to balance the rest of my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's try to discuss a couple different incidents. In your modified air bomb report, you discuss two impacts in the area of Hrasnica on 7 April and 1 July 1995. These two impacts occurred on the same street about 200 metres apart from one another; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which incident do you mean? If you would be so kind as to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm referring to G-10 and what you've described as the 1 July 1995 event.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The trajectories on both occasions came from the direction of Ilidza; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P582 for the witness. And if we could please have page 2 of the original; the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the UNMO report related to the impact on 7 April 1995. Toward the end of the report, the report reads: "The UNMOs heard the weapon coming (it landed approximately 200 metres from the team location) but did not see it in flight." Did you consider the proximity of the UNMOs' position to the locations where the modified air bombs impacted on the 7th of April and on the 1st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree that UNMOs being there as military observers would be aware of the military locations and targets in their area of observation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please now go to Exhibit D01268, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I want to focus just a little bit further on incident G-10. You indicate that you feel that this was a FAB-100 modified air bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please go to page 15 of the B/C/S of the investigative file and page 9 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the forensic report on the traces found at the scene. I want to direct your attention to the second full paragraph from the top of the page before you, this is the bottom paragraph in the English version, where the report discusses some of the metal parts and states: "According to the sign ABY-3 T, 350 written on a metal part, it was established that it belonged to a part of an electro-pyrotechnical fuse of a FAB-250 aircraft bomb of Russian origin." The fact is is that the physical traces of this impact show that there was a 250-kilogram aircraft bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the traces on the ground, we estimated that it could not have been a 250-kilo bomb and we described that in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All of the contemporaneous VRS documents related to this incident indicate it was a 250-kilogram air bomb, and I'd refer the Chamber to P591 and P1048. The commander of the VRS Brigade who fired this very modified aircraft bomb on 7 April testified in this case, at page 23196, that it was a 250 kilogram aircraft bomb. I put it to you that you're wrong and all the evidence shows that it was a 250-kilogram aircraft bomb. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I cannot accept the first line of this finding here in the first paragraph, which refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please answer the question. The question was whether you accept that the evidence referred to by Mr. Weber, whether you accept that that evidence, which apparently clearly states that it was a 250-kilogram bomb, whether you accept that you be wrong in view of that evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't accept it, regardless of what is written in this report, because all of it contradicts the action at target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Weber did not refer you or certainly did not refer you exclusively to this report. He referred to contemporaneous documents and he referred to the commander, I think, whose unit had fired a bomb who had said that it was a 250-kilogram aerial bomb. In light of that, and please don't change the question in your answers, in light of that, do you accept that you're wrong? That was Mr. Weber's question and could you please answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have exhibit numbers, Your Honour, but can we have more precise quotations so we can check? Really, we are not able to check because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Lukic, if you think that the quotations are wrong, then have you an opportunity in re-examination to deal with that. Could you please answer the question, Witness, whether in light of the evidence as told to you came to this Chamber, whether you are wrong or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody testified that he had fired that bomb on that day at that location, I have reason to believe that he was not telling the truth because the effect at target and all the traces speak differently. There remains the possibility if somebody really accurately stated that he had done it, the probability exists, but then it's -- runs completely counter to the traces on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would re-tender the investigative file right now, D1268 which is currently marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Re --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I tender it into evidence, if the counsel [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is -- just given a couple moment -- days, I think, for counsel to check the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is anything -- I'm sorry, is anything added to our pages or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's the same thing that was uploaded the other day under the 65 ter number, so counsel has been given an opportunity check it, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Until the end of this week. Today is not the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, it's tendered. We give the Defence an opportunity to revisit the matter this week, and we'll -- yes, D1268. D1268 is now admitted into evidence, and the Chamber will hear any further comments made this week or any further observations made by the Defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just about to start another incident quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we move to another incident, we should first take the break. Ms. Subotic, we take a break of 20 minutes, and we'd -- you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might have inadvertently spoke. I meant to say "P1048," not "D1048," in terms of my reference to the VRS -- one of the VRS exhibits. Just if that clarifies matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope it does. We take a break, and we resume at ten minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, I wanted to give the calculation to the Registrar in order to be translated. There's a little bit of text on it. And could that be done with urgency so that we have it before the witness leaves. And then I leave it to the parties, after they've received a copy -- and perhaps, Mr. Lukic, you can already look at the original so that if Madam Registrar would make a copy for you already so that you are in the advantageous position to be the first. And then I leave it to the parties what evidentiary value they'd like to attach to it, and perhaps the Chamber would put on the record what the outcome of the calculations is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I'd now like to direct your attention to the impact in Hrasnica on 1 July, 1995. This is the modified air bomb that hit Aleksa Santica Street number 50. The location of this impact was further away from the Aleksa Santic school than incident G-10; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that incident G-10?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct, G-10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 103 of your modified air bomb report, which is a very -- well, it's a one sentence, you state that no one was killed or wounded in this incident. And looking down at the footnote, 407, we see that you're saying this on the basis of a BiH official report, number 19/10-4-116/95. This information is not true; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not saying that. If so, would you please indicate to me what it is that is not right. The reference or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, before do you that, can you just make sure that you're transcribed correctly in your question. I thought you said you state that no one was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. The entire paragraph reads: "No one was killed or wounded in this incident."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's not an accurate statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33140 for the witness. And if we could please go to page 2 of the B/C/S and page 1 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the BiH official report under the same number you reference in your footnote dated 4 July, 1995. The first paragraph refers to the incident on 1 July and states: "Two persons were seriously and 11 slightly wounded in the explosion. The damage to the apartment buildings was also great." And if you could -- you could probably see it in the version before you, but you can see that this report goes on to individually list all of these individuals by name, and this is going on in the English version, and it describes whether or how their injuries were treated.
