This file also includes medical certificates of the victims. The report -- the information in your report is not accurate; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this day, there were several incident, I think. Are you sure that this list of wounded and injured persons pertains to Aleksa Santica 50 exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, it --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you're right on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, we see that in the first paragraph that it does. We also see that this is the exact report that you specifically rely upon for this incident.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the building in Aleksa Santica 50, there is no major damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's not about damage to buildings. It is, and that's what Mr. Weber put to you, you are relying on a report in footnote 40 -- what is 407 or 408 which is exactly the same report that this one, where Mr. Weber quotes people injured are mentioned. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one was injured at this address and in this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is that you referred to this report when you state that no one was injured or killed. The report says otherwise. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see the entire report, and it is quite possible that -- that there's some confusion there, but I do know that -- I mean, perhaps we have the wrong reference, but I don't think that's the case either. Could I please take some of your time now in order to read this calmly? No one was killed or injured in this incident and no major damage was sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is third paragraph. Third paragraph you will find the place where people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you can deal with that in re-examination. If Mr. Weber is -- would -- well, I leave it. Please move on, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 23 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is one of the statements of one of the individuals in the file who lived in one of the houses that was damaged by the explosion. Towards the end of the statement, and I'll read it verbatim, this individual states: "There are no military facilities near my family house. The Hrasnica-based UN Military Observers were quartered in the house next door, and some of them were also injured." UN military observers were injured as part of this incident; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right but that happened in Bunicki Potok, 150 metres away, not at Aleksa Santica 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 33140 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 33140 receives Exhibit P7565, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to go through a couple other quick matters before I end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to know whether the Prosecution accepts that it's not Aleksa Santica - should I deal with it or not? - but Bunicki Potok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can deal with it re-examination if you wish. Mr. Weber is aware of the issue you raised. You say it's a different incident. I leave it to Mr. Weber whether to address it. And if he doesn't, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's one event. Just so it's clear what I am referring to, it's entitled "Case 10" in the expert's report as Aleksa Santic number 50 in Hrasnica, and there's a broad statement that says no one was killed or wounded in the incident. So whether it's one occasion or the other is -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you can deal with it with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But don't argue at this moment. Either do something with it or leave it to Mr. Lukic to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's discuss incident G-13 quickly. Last week at transcript page 39517, you stated: "Evident here are traces of a small-calibre projectile coming in from the top according to the traces on the facade, which indicates that it could be a mortar projectile from a distance of 10 to 15 metres from the building." Are you saying in this event that a mortar crew set up a mortar immediately below a building and fired it into the building while they would still be right below it within the blast radius of the explosion? Are you really saying this is what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's what happened. They took the wrong elements --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not understand the rest. Could the speaker please be asked to slow down and re-start. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down and start your answer again. You said they took the wrong elements, and could you repeat what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said: Yes, correct. They took the wrong elements for firing and they hit a building instead of shooting over the building, which I assume was their intention because such traces can be left on a vertical wall only by a mortar projectile that has an upward trajectory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your theory on incident G-13 is that the modified air bomb did not directly hit the apartment building but it first ricochetted from a roof from what you claim to be the original target, the RTV building; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 50, you write that the distance between the RTV building and the apartment building is approximately 620 metres, and the difference in height is approximately 45 metres. First, the apartment building is, in fact, higher in elevation than the RTV building; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the building has 1, 2, 3, 4 -- 5 floors. I did not compare anything, but it's a five-storey building and it's as being as it is. I haven't got any other estimate. But at any rate, it's a five-storey building and we provided all the information relevant for the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the building, just to we have it clearly on the record, that you're referring to is the building that was impacted not the RTV building; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, just for me to better understand. Higher in elevation, did you mean the height of the building or did you also include the elevation on which the building was?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both. Yes, because the witness apparently may have understood the question in such a way that she only was thinking about the dimensions of the building rather than the position of the building in terms of elevation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I don't know if that clarifies things for you, but the building on Safeta Hadzica Street sits elevated and then -- than the RTV building; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to understand what you're saying happened here according to the trajectory that you're saying it was originally intended to target the RTV building. Are you saying that a modified air bomb came towards the RTV building, hit the RTV somewhere on its roof, and then went off to the right and upward by 620 metres or so to hit the -- the location Safeta Hadzica number 52? Is that -- is that what you're saying happened here?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I listen to you I would say, no, but the answer is yes. This is what actually happened: On the roof of C there was a ricochet, that is clear, and the traces can be seen very clearly. And after the ricochet on the roof of studio C, it's 0 - I don't know what height - there was this ricochet. After 600 metres this projectile that ricochetted in the direction where it left a trace on the roof of studio C, it hit the building in Safeta Hadzica. We carried out analysis that involved the following --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the angles of ricochet, the co-ordinates, everything, and on that basis we checked things and we came to the conclusion that FAB-100 and FAB-250 for all angles of ricochet are over 10 degrees, can hit this building where the modified air bomb fell at Safeta Hadzica 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree with me that modified air bomb projectiles don't spin or rotate in the same way as an artillery shell; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, just I was looking through some of the materials that you cite - for example, the marines manual in footnote 4 00 - and it appears to me that your theory that the modified air bomb would spin off to the right in a ricochet is actually based on a theory that applies to artillery and its rotation. Do I understand that correctly? That's what you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you sure that you're discussing this case with me? There is no turn to the right here. There is a trace here on studio C and there is this direction of ricochet that is clearly indicated on the roof of studio C. There is no turning to the right. I think you're talking about another incident now that we can discuss, but that pertains to Safeta Hadzica 50, I think, and after the modified air bomb went through the ground. After that, since it remained without a motor, it Bunicki Potok. I think that you've moved on to a different incident and you're talking about this one. It's true that both of them were in Safeta Hadzica, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have not, ma'am. But what maybe we can agree on right now is that -- that for -- it wouldn't be accurate to say that a modified air bomb, because it doesn't rotate like an artillery shell, it wouldn't be right to say that that could ricochet at a rather steep or a significant angle to the right; right? Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you found this turn to the right in this incident. That's my question. That's why I cannot give you an answer. And the second answer is this rotation that you keep referring to -- I mean, there are two types of rotation: Minor and major rotation; stabilizing rotation and stabilisation with fins. Neither has anything to do with ricochet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A modified air bomb wouldn't ricochet like an artillery shell; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether a projectile would ricochet or not does not depend on whether it's a modified air bomb or anything else. It depends on the configuration of its external shape and its angle of descent. You can totally exclude a modified air bomb as a special problem for ricochet because quite simply it doesn't depend on the construction of the projectile. It depends on the angle of descent and also the external shape of the projectile. These are the parameters that define ricochet. The angle of ricochet is determined by these two parameters: The angle of descent and the external shape of the projectile. So it can be any projectile. It will certainly ricochet at one point in time. And in a certain way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that based on the shapes -- the relative shapes of an artillery shell and an air bomb that they would possibly ricochet in a similar manner?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every one of them in their own way and every one will ricochet. It's a process, as we all know, and this is something that is not described analytically but experimentally. We mastered this very well. So this is something that we can count on, and we restrict elements for firing so that projectiles would not fall into angles of ricochet so that they could accurately hit the target involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understood Mr. Weber's question well, he asked you whether it would be possible after ricochet to -- that the projectile hits finally a structure at an altitude of 600 metres higher -- or is that further? Then I misunderstood him. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In reviewing your modified air bomb report, you describe the amount of damage to many different locations. The -- this appears to be based on what you found in the investigative materials related to the ditch incidents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We analysed the parameters that we had, we analysed the firing power of both bombs, we analysed the experimental results that were finally cited by our colleague, Mr. Zecevic, and on that basis we provided the findings that we provided. utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have any contact or communications of any kind with Mile Poparic since you started your testimony two weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have breakfast together every morning, but we do not communicate about this work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you had -- and when you say "every morning," you've had breakfast with him every single day since you started your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, today we didn't have breakfast together and perhaps that happened on another day or two, but usually we do have breakfast together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there -- it's -- at this time I would not have further questions. However, that's with the understanding that the investigative materials related to the modified air bomb incidents would be admitted into evidence. If could I read those numbers on the record just right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That would be the -- I'm going to skip D1268, which was already used. D1270 MFI; 65 ter 33107; 65 ter 33108; 65 ter 33109; 65 ter 33110, which is actually the remaining investigative materials from G-15; 65 ter 10208; 65 ter 33131. This is a date where we don't -- where we did not put this in because we've dropped those incidents but we'd be seeking to tender that document at this time.

utterances.text: Before -- Mr. Weber, the first document you mentioned was D1270, MFI. Have we got up to D1270 in this case? The thought the last one was D1268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I give you an opportunity to re-examine the witness, Mr. Lukic, I would have a few questions. Witness, this is figure 43 of your report. You have plotted northerly direction, and you have plotted the azimuth of Spasenije Cane Babovic Street. If you would translate the compass bearing of that street in more northerly direction, what would the compass bearing be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the upper part of the street which looks like taking a turn? Is that what you mean? North of the point where I worked or all the way up there?

utterances.text: No. I'm just asking about the -- that part of the street where the yellow dot is, in southerly compass bearing is 157 degrees. Now in the opposite direction, what would be the compass bearing of that same portion of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the opposite direction, if it would be measured from M -- N - sorry - up to this same line on the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would be the compass bearing in degrees if you don't look in downwards direction of that part of the street but rather look in upward direction and still the street where the yellow dot is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be 360 minus 23. If I can do the math quickly if my head, that would be 337.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's 157 plus 180, so I have no comment on that. Could we now move to another picture of the same street in the same document; that is, page 97 in English and page 96 in B/C/S. That's the same street, isn't it, we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And that's the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you testified that the yellow line, which indicates the origin -- the direction of the origin of fire would be at an angle of initially you said 10 to 20 degrees, later you took it a bit broader and you said 10 to 30 degrees. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that would be very close to the north/south direction, regardless of whether it's 10, 20, or 30. We did not restrict it that way. It's just close to north/south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take it step by step. If it would be 10, what would be the compass bearing of the yellow line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be 100 -- 157 minus 200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You earlier said that in this direction it was 337. Would that be 337 plus 10?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that there is some wrong translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then take it again. If the curb stone is as you said earlier at 337, if the yellow line would be at an angle of 10 degrees, then that line would have what compass bearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would expect, as a matter of fact, 347. That is, 337 plus 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it would be 20 degrees, what would it be, the compass bearing of the yellow line, if it was at an angle of 20 degrees from the compass bearing of the street itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 337, 360, that would be very close to the north. Maybe it would cross over by 1 degree to the east. Yes, it would be north. 337 plus 20, that's 357; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's still west, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very close to the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still west of north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if it would be 30 degrees, then what would be the bearing of the yellow line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 367; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we usually call 7 degrees because we start anew at north, isn't it? Now you earlier said - and I asked you whether you were sure about it - you said it's obviously east from north. Is it? The whole of the range you gave that goes from 347, if it is 10 degrees, up to 7 degrees, if it would have been 30 degrees, an angle of 30 degrees. You said it's east of north, and I asked you whether you were sure about it. You said yes, you are. I'm again asking you whether the bearing, compass bearing, of this direction of origin of fire in your own analysis would always be in the east of north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because at the point where the incident happened, we observe where the projectile had arrived from, then in my only analysis, that's in the greatest proximity to north/south direction. Looking from the point where the incident happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's not what you testified. You said it was east of north and I asked whether you were sure about it. You said you were. Do you want to correct yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe just a little. But that is, for all intents and purposes, north/south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I think from your previous answers, I took it that the range, in a bit of a rough assessment, perhaps, the range of compass bearings for this yellow line would be between 347 and 07 degrees. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we analysed it a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that in the middle of this range we'd be at 352; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's west from north; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your report, we read that the BiH positions were from strict north to -- well, quite a bit further down in easterly direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, your conclusion that it would have been fired from BiH-controlled territory was based on that territory to be found from north to east of north. And where you said obviously, the direction of the origin of fire was east of north. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Or the direction north/south. I mean, it's closer to the south than to -- sorry. It's closer to north than to north-east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's west of north, isn't it? Let me rephrase this question. In the previous questions, I think you concluded that the -- most of the range of the compass bearing of the yellow line was in the area west of north and only a smaller portion was east of north. You agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 61 of your report, you say it's obvious because it was fired east of north - and let me just -- Could we have paragraph 61, I think, is immediately following this figure. It's a really -- in English, we need to go to the next page. Could we go not next page in English. Yes, I think -- still the beginning was on the previous page but we couldn't see it. Could we go back briefly. And could we zoom in on the lower part, 61. You said that anything from north to 67 degrees was BiH-held territory. Could we now move to the next page in both versions and zoom in on the top part. And that, by the way, is illustrated in figure 52a. Your conclusion is: "It is obvious" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First we -- now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "It is obvious that all the directions from the north to the azimuth of 67 degrees pass through the territory that is controlled by the BH army." That is from 0 degrees to, as plotted, 66, but as described, 67 degrees. Now if you correct your conclusion that the yellow line which is the origin -- the direction of the origin of fire is not east from north but more prominently west from north, would that in any way affect your conclusion as to where this shell may have come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, we did not deal with detail the deviation of the strip from the curb. We just concluded that it's an angle less than 90 degrees. So it's an acute angle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. You testified that it was your assessment that it was between 10 and 20 degrees. If you want me to go to the transcript page, we'll do that. And then later, because you said it was a bit rough, you broadened it to 10 to 30 degrees. Your testimony was not that it was less than 90. Your testimony was initially that it was 10 to 20, and then that it was 10 to 30. On the basis of this, do you also revise that it's all obvious that the shell must have come from an area which was BiH-controlled area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I clumsily estimated these angles when I gave my answer. They look very acute. But just to be completely safe, we took it only as an acute angle less than 90 degrees and that's how we analysed it in this paper precisely in order to avoid arriving at this analysis that we made today. My estimate would be 10, then 20, then 30, even 40, is it so, or isn't it so, that's we just put it in as an acute angle. So I still stand by what I said: That the safest estimate we could give is the one we gave in the paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you gave your testimony in this courtroom, and that's just as important, and there you limited to 10 to 30 per cent. Now, you also said on the basis of that assessment that the origin of fire was east from north. Do you revise that conclusion on the basis of your own estimate that the angle with the compass bearing of the street would be between 10 and 30 degrees? Do you revise your conclusion it would be east of north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My estimate based on this picture here in the courtroom, I'm afraid it's not completely safe, and I have to stand by the answer that I gave before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you whether you want to revise the estimate. My question is whether you want to revise on the basis of the estimate - right or wrong - that the origin of fire, the direction of the origin of fire, was east of north.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our own analysis here, now, was the same relative to the north. The one we just discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We would ask to have P7548 on our screens, please. Actually, no, I would start from -- I'm sorry. It's the Prosecution exhibit and it does not have all the pages we need. So we need 1D01293, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 16 in B/C/S; 11 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go back to the other page again. The previous one, Mr. Lukic. In English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, now I see it, yes. Could we enlarge slightly. Let me just have a look. Yes, I've seen it. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm still looking for M56.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So can we go now to page 16 in B/C/S and 11 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the basic data for ammunition here. Also we see M49, M62, M56. I just want to draw your attention to this, and then I would like to move to page 24 in B/C/S and 13 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I asked -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did ask for new pages, yes. And there they are, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see under point 4, gunpowder charges. Item 55 says that the propellant powder charge for 120-millimetre M74 mortar shells is comprised of the primary and increment charges. Only with the primary charge firing does not take place. Why is that so; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is because it's a heavier shell, a large shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of item 57, which is on the next page. In paragraph 2, it says: "The charge comes fitted into the shell stabiliser and it does not require any preparation before firing." Page 26 in B/C/S and 15 in English, please. When you discuss the M62 shell, specifically: "M62 P3, M62 P3, M56 P1, and M62 P2, M64 light smoke shells, and the M66 illumination shells, they come with charges fitted onto the shell during the production and do not require any preparation before firing." As opposed to this -- actually, does this correspond to what you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the primary charge on this shell, is it screwed on during the -- at the positions or is there such a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for these shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 64 now. That is on page 26 in B/C/S and page 15 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are we looking at this in general or in relation to a certain incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To a certain incident, Your Honour, and two artefacts we saw here in the courtroom, and there was a discussion whether that basic charge should be dealt with somewhere in the field or not. And it was presented to Ms. Subotic actually that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it could be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could remind me, that was what kind of a shell exactly? What number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: M62. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here in paragraph 64 what is discussed are M49 shells, and it says -- we see it's that shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version, we need to move onto the next page; and also in English version, we need to move onto the next page. That's where the text continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So for M49 at the top of the page, the first bullet point in B/C/S and in English, it says: "One primary charge, packed in the same box as the fuse and placed in the designated slot inside the shell crate." As for this shell, M49, is it necessary to mount the primary charge?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is put into the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this shell look different when one looks at it compared to M62?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. Just if we look at them at the same time, they all vary, but it doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These shells that you looked at in relation to the Markale incidents, it says that they're M62. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's some variations here of M62 but we're not going to deal with that any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, we would like to tender this document because it is more comprehensive. We would like to have it admitted need, and we can link it up to what the Prosecution already tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can do that. Have you done it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we haven't because we cannot merge anything with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering what we should do at this moment, whether we should reserve a number or provisionally admit. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's some paragraphs missing, and we believe that those could impact on the relevance of some of the information that was presented. So as a general matter, we've no objection to the admission of manuals. So if there's a provisional number that can be assigned, that's no problem, but if we could please discuss what portions of this should be maybe additionally translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are willing to have the whole manual. We have no problem. If anything is missing...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I leave it to counsel what he wants to translate. We might have a couple extra paragraphs that we would like to have translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the problems is if you do not deal with certain pages of the manual, Chambers staff will then to go through all that if you have not clearly defined. At the same time, of course, we should also be careful not to lose context. For the time being let's reserve a number for the whole of this manual, and then the parties could sit together and see what is relevant or not so as to save unnecessary work for us as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I didn't want anything to be misunderstood that we think that it's been linked up to what was used by the Prosecution as of now, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be reserved.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1278, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's for the manual on this 120-millimetre mortar shells. It's -- we know the 65 ter number. It's therefore not only reserved but it's MFI'd, and we'll later hear what portions we really will have to look at. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, it was put to that you had you problems in terms of perspective because you used photographs from police documents. How did you redress that? Actually, I cannot ask you directly.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Problems of perspective, because you used photographs from police files.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem of perspective is one that we practically did not have to resolve by special methods. Where it was necessary to resolve it, we used programmes and we carried out many analyses on the spot, and then we compiled photo documentation about that, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what you wished to say? Markale I and II were discussed, and what was mentioned was that one mortar shell fell in both places. I don't know whether you can tell me now, but how many mortar shells are needed in order to destroy a target? I'm referring to 120-millimetres or 82-millimetres; that would be the calibre?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is tactical information. Right this minute, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly take a look at 1D1293.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it the same D1278 MFI?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, yeah. Page 57. Can we have this one enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were already asked about this. Judge Orie asked you about this. He asked you whether you took into account minus 500. That is to say, a 500 metre difference in altitude.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that we did not and that there was no need for that because we analysed this throughout the horizontal plane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, a couple of things. I'd just -- in order for follow -- we've discussed many, many incidents, and things have come up at different times. If we could please have a precise reference to where things were made so that we can track what the actual testimony was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you assist both Mr. Weber and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, not at this moment, I'm sorry. I have cut out something completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll try to finds it ourselves, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that there was no need for that. On this table, can minus 500 be seen?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If counsel could just state for the record -- I see that the type of mortar is on the page, an M74, but I'm not sure what the break -- actually, what type of mortar shell this table refers to, and there's no translation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only can see that it's first charge -- give me one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the top of what we see is 120-millimetre M74, is that -- apparently with a 130-millimetre per seconds initial speed. That's what with he can see from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just going to leave this vague. But to state my concern, I'm concerned we're possibly not looking at the right type of mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you have any better mortar for us to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on and I'll come back, obviously. I have some ... I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll come back to this one. Can we have 1D5756 now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who took this photograph? The one before you, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken by my colleague, Mile Poparic, and myself when we visited in September, the 17th of September, in Vase Miskina. We did this as instructed by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was your finding? How big are these tiles?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I've already said, that it is squares and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have some foundation? We have when, where. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was in response to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Otherwise, we are just talking about a file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was in response to a request of I then take it the Karadzic Trial Chamber or any other Chamber? When was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says 17th of September. Only year is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 17 September of what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2010 in the street of Vase Miskina. I did say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Mr. Weber asked you about what he -- actually about what Mirza Sabljica marked during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05544. Could we please take a look at that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just -- are we moving to a different incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record the relevance of this photo is unclear to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Mr. Lukic, we're moving now to which incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Klare Cetkin Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You used this photograph in your report.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph is one that we dealt with as photo documentation in terms of measuring traces on the spot in Klare Cetkin Street. So we used it for verification for what we measured on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you present when this photograph was marked?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the courtroom when Witness Mirza Sabljica testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D1405 on our screens now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the transcript of Mr. Sabljica's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 22 in e-court, please. Should correspond to page 7-8 ... the next one then, please. Should correspond to page 7834 of the Karadzic transcript. And then from line 12, it starts -- line 20, the question was: "Do you see that this crater here is right next to the pavement. One bit of the pavement even had to be replaced and repaired. "A. That's clearly visible."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, but just to [indiscernible] -- the -- the phrase immediately above, it's relevant for the context of this photograph. If counsel wouldn't mind starting at line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If would you follow the suggestion, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are free to do so. Of course, otherwise Mr. Weber will revisit the matter in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because it was clear later. I will just need to read more, but that's fine. Page 16: "Q. Do you know this place?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Line 16. What did I say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Page."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Line 16. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Q. Do you know this place? "A. Looking at this photograph it could be anywhere in the city of Sarajevo because I can't see the buildings around, so I couldn't even tell you in which part of town it is based on this photograph." And then after that, I already read. Then Mr. Sabljica was shown several other documents in Karadzic case like 1D2576, and it was -- he was informed that it's regarding G-6 incident. On page 7844, from lines 18 to 22, 23, 24, and then he was shown this photograph which was marked in Karadzic case as 1D2440. And now we need page 7846 for this transcript, so we have to go 12 pages ahead. Line 9, Mr. Sabljica was asked, I quote: "Sir, can you now recognise the heating plant at Alipasino Polje and this same spot, a portion of the sidewalk that had been replaced and also the pavement that was repaired? "A. Yes, I do, but now it's taken from a different angle. "Q. Would you agree with me that this photo was taken from outside the building where -- bearing the memorial plaque? "A. Yes, I do agree based on the replacement of the sidewalk I could agree with that." And then they were -- talked -- they talked about the photograph at line 25, starts the question: "Thank you. Can you now please tell us whether this measuring," end of quote, and we have to go to next page. I quote: "... band was placed in the way that you would place the band to indicate the major axis. "A. Yes, but we did mark all the traces and based on the photograph it is my assumption that this could be indicating the direction from which the projectile had come in."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to object based on the fact that he just jumped the discussion about the major axis in the preceding page. I'm worried that this is being misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. I'm afraid that it escapes my understanding what exactly your problem is, Mr. Weber. And could you do it in such a way that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will try to do it in a general way. There was a photo that's been shown that was marked with the witness that did have a location, which is referred to on the previous page which Mr. Sabljica was commenting on in terms of the major axis and him being able or not able to determine that major axis based on that photograph that we saw which counsel is relying upon. I think if counsel is going to do that, we should have the full discussion about the reference points that Mr. Sabljica is being able to comment or not comment upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it at this moment in the hands of Mr. Lukic, and if there's any error made there, then have you an opportunity -- because I'm just a bit lost. You're referring to a lot of things which we haven't read, so therefore I'm unable to follow it. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed but for not more than one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I have to go back now in the transcript as well because the picture was first marked and then he was explained where this whole picture was taken. And so we have to go back to page 7834 in the transcript, which is 13 pages back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will you able to do this exercise in one or two minutes or -- if not, then we should stop. I take it we go back and I -- from what I saw a minute ago was it that Mr. Sabljica initially said, "I don't know where it is," and then later that was apparently in one way or another was resolved. I'd like the parties to sit together and to see how they divide their time tomorrow. We need at least half an hour, if not a little bit more, for other matters. Ms. Subotic, this is the last time I'm going to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate because the Chamber considers it -- that your testimony should be concluded by tomorrow. Therefore, also if you want to serve the interests of justice best, then it would also be best to immediately answer to the questions, because otherwise some questions may not be able to be put, which would be a pity. You may follow the usher, and you should not discuss your evidence with anyone or communicate about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 8th of October, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.
